title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes (Q1 2027)
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Overview:

Summary:
Unified Inference is Redwood's next-generation product initiative to provide a single, consistent developer experience and runtime for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, key design specs, roadmap and themes for the next three quarters, pricing & packaging guidance, and release notes for the v1.0 launch (internal release).

Goals and Success Criteria:
- Business goals: 1) Increase hosted API ARR by 25% in 12 months via improved performance & clearer packaging; 2) Grow Dedicated commitments by enabling predictable throughput SLAs; 3) Open 3 strategic Private deals in regulated verticals by end of Q3 2027.
- Product metrics: 1) 99.95% availability for tiered Hosted endpoints; 2) median token latency <= 60ms for short-form generation (<=256 tokens) on default models; 3) reduce per-token cost by 15% for top-20% of customer workloads via optimize recommendations.
- Acceptance criteria: documented API surface parity across deployment modes, validated end-to-end canary rollout flow, pricing page and self-serve billing integration live, end-to-end e2e tests and 50+ customer QA prompts validated.

Target personas:
- ML Engineers integrating inference into product features (primary)
- Platform Engineers consuming Dedicated/Private capacity (secondary)
- Solutions & Sales teams evaluating enterprise requirements (supporting audience)

PRD: Requirements (MUST / SHOULD / MAY)
1) Core API & Surface (MUST)
- Single REST/SDK spec exposing: generate, chat, embeddings, rerank, and stream endpoints.
- Function/tool-calling primitives for structured tool calls.
- Model catalog with model id, version, architecture metadata, and compatibility flags.
- Authentication and rate-limiting consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

2) Deployment Parity (MUST)
- Same config semantics (model pinning, rollout policy, fallback routing) across Hosted, Dedicated, Private.
- Private deployments must support customer KMS integration and audit logging.

3) Performance & Cost Controls (MUST)
- Batching configuration with latency targets and throughput controls.
- KV/prefix caching primitives and auto cache hints from the SDK.
- Quantization profile registry and rollout controls for model variants.

4) Observability & SLOs (SHOULD)
- Per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, traceable request ids.
- Automated alerting for 5xx spikes and tail-latency regressions.

5) Quality & Guardrails (SHOULD)
- Built-in regression tests tied to prompt suites, quality scorecard per model.
- Safety/PII detection checks in pipeline for Private/Enterprise workloads.

6) Pricing & Packaging (MUST)
- Usage-based hosted pricing with explicit per-token generation & embedding rates.
- Dedicated: monthly reserved capacity tiers with burst options and overage rules.
- Private: licensing + support tiers; optional enterprise packaging for on-prem SKU.

Design Specs (Key Decisions)
- API: Maintain OpenAPI v3 spec; canonical SDK will expose convenience clients for Python/Node/Go. Use JSON schema for model outputs and function call payloads.
- Runtime routing: Implement policy layer that supports priority-based routing (latency/cost/region/tier). Policy config stored in central config service and versioned.
- Caching: Two-level cache design: 1) Request-prefix KV cache on serving nodes (low-latency); 2) Shared hashed prefix cache RPC for warm-starts. Cache invalidation governed by TTL + model-rollout hooks.
- Quantization & Model Variants: Registry of quantization profiles (fp16, int8, awq variants). Runtime supports transparent fallback to full-precision variant for high-quality paths.
- Rollouts: Canary by traffic slices, with automatic rollback on quality or latency regression. Canary policy evaluates: 95th token latency, failure rate, and quality degradation measured against seeded prompts.

Roadmap & Themes (Q1 2027 - Q3 2027)
- Q1 2027 (Beta): API parity, model catalog, Hosted billing integration, canary rollout plumbing, v1 SDKs.
- Q2 2027 (GA for Hosted): Performance tuning (latency SLOs), per-route dashboards, pricing & self-serve billing, initial Dedicated tiers (small/medium/large).
- Q3 2027 (Dedicated & Private focus): Dedicated SLA commitments, Private deployment GA (VPC + basic KMS integration), enterprise packaging, sales enablement materials.

Roadmap milestones and owners:
- API parity and SDKs - owner: eng-developer-experience; target: 2027-02-15.
- Runtime routing & caching - owner: eng-serving-runtime; target: 2027-03-30.
- Billing & pricing pages - owner: finance-and-legal + product; target: 2027-04-15.
- Dedicated capacity launch (tiers & SLA) - owner: eng-sre + eng-infra; target: 2027-05-31.
- Private deployment GA - owner: eng-private-deployments; target: 2027-07-31.

Pricing & Packaging Notes
- Hosted pricing (recommended list):
  - Generation: $0.003 per 1K prompt tokens, $0.012 per 1K generated tokens (example tiered).
  - Embeddings: $0.0007 per 1 embedding (128-d default).
  - Monthly free tier: 100K prompt tokens + 10K generated tokens for new orgs.
- Dedicated: Monthly reserved instances priced by reserved vGPU hours + unit of throughput (tokens/s). Include 10% discount for annual commit, burst capacity at 1.5x reserved throughput billed at overage rates.
- Private: Base license fee + per-node support fee; pricing template shared with sales and legal.
- Packaging guidance: Encourage self-serve Hosted for small teams; Dedicated for customers needing predictable throughput and SLAs; Private for regulated customers. Offer migration credits and tooling to move from Hosted to Dedicated/Private with model-sidepin compatibility.

Release Notes - v1.0 (internal launch)
- Release date: 2027-01-10 (internal beta)
- Highlights:
  - Unified REST API with generate/chat/embeddings/rerank endpoints.
  - Model catalog v1 with 12 curated models and version metadata.
  - Canary rollout plumbing and automatic rollback on perf or quality regressions.
  - v1 SDKs for Python and Node with streaming support.
  - Initial pricing page and billing integration for Hosted.
- Known issues:
  - Edge-case tail latency > target on mixed-batch workloads when sequence length variance is high (tracked in eng-serving-runtime/known-issues).
  - Private deployment KMS automation (customer onboarding) is manual during beta.

Rollout & Launch Plan
1) Internal beta (Jan 2027): Enable 20 pilot orgs (mix of startups and mid-market) via invitation; collect performance telemetry and customer QA prompts.
2) External limited beta (Mar 2027): Open self-serve signup with usage caps; publish pricing and docs.
3) GA (Hosted) (May 2027): Remove caps, enable billing for all orgs; publish SLA and runbooks.
4) Dedicated & Private GA (staged by capacity) (June-Aug 2027).

Operational SLOs and Monitoring
- Availability: 99.95% per-region for Hosted.
- Latency: median <= 60ms, p95 <= 250ms for <=256 token generate on default model.
- Error budget policy and alerting: priority-1 for >=0.5% 5xx within 15 min window.
- Monitoring: per-route traces, token-level cost reports, model quality regression dashboards.

Security & Compliance Highlights
- Private deployments must integrate customer KMS.
- Audit logging of model inference requests for Dedicated/Private.
- Data residency options per region tile; default retention 30 days for Hosted telemetry.

Open Risks and Mitigations
- Risk: High tail latency for variable-length workloads. Mitigation: fine-grained batching heuristics and adaptive scheduling + model padding heuristics.
- Risk: Customer confusion across packaging. Mitigation: clear decision matrix and migration playbook in sales enablement.
